nodes.label: B-070: Work Order's Stale S2 Instruction Corrected; Fresh Authorization Left Open
nodes.description: Lane B finding: after B-068/B-069 closed Verified at 335564e, docs/LANE-B-WORK-ORDER.md S2.2d still told Lane B the historical D-164/D-165 human-T5/agent-T6 packet was its next code unit -- but D-171 held that packet pending the target order, and D-175 through D-181 later decided and corrected the target order without ever lifting the hold. Verifying a handoff record is not the same act as authorizing a build. Lane A corrected the immediate hazard: S2.2d now carries a historical/held notice, the next-code-unit claim is removed, and the section points to this handoff and V1-PHASE-CLOSURE.md S5 instead. The Chief Editor was asked whether a fresh bounded S2 authorization should be recorded now (a no-route-enablement T5/T6 control unit) or held until all six UNVERIFIED operation shapes in the factory-route-operation-crosswalk (including OP-FINAL-SIGNOFF, which has no R at all in source) are resolved, and asked for both options to be drafted for Lane B's independent review rather than one being selected yet. Neither option is applied; no new decision record was written, Modular_PRD/Build-Spec/Register are untouched, and Lane B's lane state stays Eligible, not Active.
nodes.rationale: A handoff record moving to Verified answers exactly the question it was raised to answer -- whether the correction was independently confirmed -- and nothing more; treating that closure as build authorization would let a superseded instruction slip past every governance layer this project's own history shows are needed precisely because a status copied into a second document is the drift mechanism this corpus keeps re-discovering.
